study type: Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
outcome: Time to skin closure (dermal and epidermal layers)
Wound complications (wound infection, hematoma, seroma, reclosure, readmission)
cohort: The study included women undergoing cesarean delivery who were participants in 26 randomized controlled trials.
finding: Absorbable suture reduced the risk of skin separation compared to staple after cesarean delivery and did not increase the risk of wound complications, though it slightly prolonged wound closure time.
mod_finding: The findings are specifically related to the choice of skin closure material during cesarean delivery, directly impacting outcomes for this mode of birth.
